stem: Which of the following is a high risk factor for vitreous hemorrhage?
Which of the following is a high risk factor for vitreous hemorrhage?
explanation_verbatim: High myopia increases the risk of vitreous hemorrhage due to retinal thinning and predisposition to retinal tears. It also raises the risk of retinal detachment.

stem:
A 70-year-old patient presents with sudden onset floaters and flashes in one eye. On examination, the red reflex is absent.
What is the most appropriate next step in management?
options: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) of the macula
explanation_verbatim: Flashes, floaters, and absent red reflex suggest retinal detachment or vitreous hemorrhage. A dilated fundus exam is essential for diagnosis and urgent management.

stem: A 22-year-old male patient presented to the ophthalmology clinic with a complaint of seeing bugs or cobwebs together with light flashes. Ophthalmoscopy revealed an evident Weiss ring. Which of the following might occur as a complication to that patient's condition?

A 22-year-old male patient presented to the ophthalmology clinic with a complaint of seeing bugs or cobwebs together with light flashes. Ophthalmoscopy revealed an evident Weiss ring. Which of the following might occur as a complication to that patient's condition?
explanation_verbatim:
This case is a case of PVD. Complications of PVD may be:
A. Traction at areas of abnormal vitreoretinal adhesions or areas of weak retina may cause retinal tears/detachment
B. Retinal tears/detachment may cause vitreous haemorrhage if a bridging retinal blood vessel is torn.
